title: Don’t think, just download it!
text:
This app has been a lifesaver for my family. Yes most of the features are things that come standard on any smartphone, however the convenience of having (almost) everything in one place has helped this busy Dad and Mom get more organized.

We downloaded this initially for the Recipe Box and Meal Planner tools (premium features). Add your favorite recipes to your recipe box, plan your meals, and it automatically adds the ingredients to your list. The amount of time we save each week on meal planning and grocery lists has been well worth the monthly fee!

There are a few features that are lacking and some I’d love to see incorporated.

99% of the time I use the app on my phone and when adding a new task or item to your list, it doesn’t allow you to categorize it until after you have submitted it, sending that to the “uncategorized” section at the bottom of the list. Being able to categorize it when you initially enter the data would save some clicks/time.

Another feature that could use an upgrade is the calendar. It’s nice being able to import your calendar, but integrating it so that you can create an event in the app and have it show up in your default calendar app would be a welcomed update. 

Add some iOS widgets (calendar, notes, todo, shopping list, etc.) 

A wishlist item would be Life360 integration or replacement. The maps is very basic and unreliable. We have noticed inaccuracy in the locations, delayed or non-existent notifications when leaving/arriving at one of our set places. Life360 is an excellent tool for not only location services, but also crash detection, driving summary, and more.

That being said. Don’t think, just download it!

title: Task editing/creation needs improvement
text: Overall this is a really cool app with so much potential to help my family be organized but the limited functionality of the task entry interface in lists prevents me from using this. If you edit a task the category to which it was assigned changes to uncategorized from whatever category you had originally tagged the task. It is a pain to recategorize because you have to click a separate button on the app or web interface to categorize a task. If the developer could make two changes this problem would be eliminated: (1) stop changing a task to “uncategorized” just because the name/title of the task is changed and (2) create a task entry interface that allows the user to (a) categorize the task at the same time that the task is created and (b) select the status of the task (undone, done, in progress, on hold) in the same interface with which the task is created (right now you have to create a task in a little field, then once the task is created you have to click another button to assign a category to the task, then click save, and click a third button to mark complete — all of this should be able to be in one interface, even if there remains a “quick add” field for adding uncategorized tasks). Hopefully the developer can add this functionality and this app would be great!

title: Fantastic sanity saving app with one issue..
text:
I’d like to start by saying how much my family loves and appreciates this app.  I have OCD, so organization and planning is a huge part of my life.  I use FamilyWall every day, and it is DEFINITELY worth the premium price.  I mainly use the calendar, meal planner, recipe box, and lists. 

The calendar is fantastic because you can change the colors to better organize each event.  You can do recurring events.  I also love the layout of events and the way it shows the colored dots on the days that have something on the calendar. 

I love the recipe box and meal planner SO MUCH.  You can write in your own recipe, or make it a million times easier by using a link from a recipe online and FamilyWall enters it in for you.  It’s so helpful to have a list already there of our favorites and even some recipes we haven’t tried yet. 

I love the lists function too because, well, OCD and lists.  Lol.  

I have recently started using the budget function, and honestly, I was shocked to be disappointed with it.  There is a glitch showing that I’m way over budget even though I have entered in my income.  The income doesn’t show up unless you switch to a different week, then back to the week you’re working on.  Even then, it sometimes doesn’t fix it.  

I also don’t like that you can’t have separate spending limits for bills vs other expenses.  I would do away with the spending limit that covers all of the categories, and just stick with the page after that that allows you to enter in spending limits individually for each category.  I’d like to have some categories that don’t have a spending limit, but it restricts that because you have to have a limit for each category or it shows over budget.  It’s kind of redundant to have to budget the bills on the budget then have to do it again on spending limits because you already know your overall limit based on your income.  For me personally, I’d rather be able to separate bills and other categories because I don’t really have a choice on how much my bills are, so there’s no point in having a “limit” for how much they’ll be. 

My last issue is that there isn’t an option for money left from the week before to carry over into the next week, so you have to enter it as “income” the next week.  This, along with the other issues, is pretty frustrating because I do love this app so much, but I think I may have to find a different app for budgeting which also means talking my family into downloading yet another app.

I will say that the budgeting function has huge potential to be great.  I love that you can choose how often it reoccurs, and you can customize the days rather than just generic options like “daily, weekly, monthly”, etc.  It’s helpful to have that function because a lot of subscriptions come out every thirty days rather than every month on the same date.  I love that it calculates how much you have left to spend.  It gives me so much peace of mind knowing how much I actually have left to spend compared to looking at my bank account which always takes days for the payments to actually show.  I know exactly how much I have left to spend with this app!

Overall, I’m extremely happy with FamilyWall.  My only complaint would be with the budgeting function, and I’m looking forward to seeing improvements to it and adding another star back to my review.  Thank you for taking the time to create an app like this!  You guys are the reason my home runs smoothly and that I’ve remained sane!

title: They turned a bathroom scale into a subscription hostage situation
text:
Do NOT buy a Withings scale in 2026.

I bought Withings hardware to measure my weight, my body fat, my BMI and send it to Apple Health, where literally every other health device I own lives. That used to be the whole point of a smart scale.

As of October 13, 2026, Withings decided that basic feature is now a rent payment. Create a new Withings account today and you cannot export your own data to Apple Health or Health Connect unless you pay for Withings+ about $100/year. Not for coaching. Not for AI insights. Not for anything new. Just to move a number the scale you already paid for measured, from their app to Apple's app.

That's not a premium feature. That's a toll booth on your own data.

And don't let the "existing users are grandfathered" line fool you that's an admission, not a defense. They know current owners would revolt if they cut us off, so they're only screwing the next buyer who won't read the fine print until after setup, when they hit a paywall screen trying to turn on Apple Health sync. Your account gets deleted, you switch phones/emails, you set up a scale for your spouse/kid/parents? Welcome to the subscription.

This ruins the product. A smart scale that doesn't freely sync to Apple Health isn't smart, it's a walled garden with a glass platform. The hardware is now irrelevant I can't recommend a product whose business model is "buy the device, then pay us forever to actually use it in your health ecosystem."

Buy an InBody instead. The InBody Dial / H20N does proper 8-electrode body composition, syncs to the InBody app, and integrates with Apple Health, Google Fit, and Samsung Health with no subscription costs to access your body composition data. You buy it, you own it, it works. Revolutionary concept.

Withings used to be the easy recommendation. Now it's an easy warning: do not buy hardware from a company that will charge you rent to export your own weight.

title: Ew user

First, they want you to sign/buy an additional care package to just obtain a copy of your own EKG. Second, the app is what I would call a POS, it just continues to LOCK UP.  I deleted it and reinstalled two time and it is still locked up. I cannot used. What good is it if the app sucks!

title: Peace of mind with Kardia
text: Kardia gives us peace of mind.  My husband had an Afib issue. Kardia identified it, even before he even did, allowing us to seek medical attention right away

title: Pleased
text: My wife is an RN BSN CCRN and I’m just a dumb orthopedic surgeon with an electric problem with my heart as a former pro athlete.  It has helped us monitor my heart and adjust the meds waiting for my procedure,

title: Misleading inclusion of PVCs, SVE, and Wide QRS.
text: I used the first generation of Kardia for a couple of years and was satisfied.  My doctor said the Apple Watch’s are just as good.  When I ran across the 6L, I thought that would be different enough (includes PVCs, SVE, and Wide QRS) to make the purchase.  It turns out you have to purchase a monthly or yearly subscription for this to work.  In my opinion, this was not clearly stated.  I feel that the company did this on purpose knowing a lot of its core base of elderly customers did not understand this.  With that, I lost all trust with Kardia.  If you can’t trust them on business practices, then why should you trust that the device is providing valuable data on the technical side?  My cardiologist told me to “save your money”.

title: Please make the HR bigger
text: Please go back to the larger HR reading display. With the new update the number is very small down on the side and hard for this senior to read.

title: Saved my Aunt
text: Bought a Kardiamobile when my Aunt experienced fatigue with activity and said she got a bit winded.  It revealed atrial fibrillation!  Went to ED and she was admitted, had a successful cardioversion, and a stroke or worse was prevented!

title: Phenomenal tool
text: I am an RN, I bought one for myself when I was having symptoms to monitor at home, covid as an ER nurse gave me some trouble short term. I’m fine now, but Anytime I was feeling bad, I would look and say my rhythm is normal, so then it’s “anxiety” which would help me rationalize and move on. I refuse to accept anxiety. Worked every time. Also, I bought my parents one so I can keep an eye on them. This thing is awesome. It’s nice to have access to a board certified cardiologist should you need one. You can track/trend your own data. It’s a great tool to have around. I love it.

title: Or expect annoying spam
text: Got this for my 90-year-old parents but the constant spamming to join the program makes it confusing for them to operate. Not sure if they’ll be able to use it by themselves because of the spam and excess advertising covering the main features of the app that are required to use it properly. It would be one thing if this was done once a month but it’s doing it literally almost done every move you make on the app. OK.

title: Good basic app
text: As a physician I was skeptical about Kardia until my cardiologist recommended I use the basic version to guard against atrial fibrillation (look it up). I’m pushing 80 and have risk of stroke, so afib is a real concern. The science on Kardia is sound and the technology is accurately advertised. It’s very easy to use, integrates with my phone and sends results to my MD and my wife. As an aside, I just discovered that my cotton picking Apple Watch detected afib two years ago and I never used that feature. The basic Kardia like mine is all you need, probably, but the 6 lead is better and they will be improving the gadgets going forward. Afib is a serious condition and if you’re a senior Kardia is a good device to use regularly. Cheers - T👍🏼

title: Buggy and dangerous
text:
I'd stopped using Garmin for cycling a few years ago because of all the bugs. But last year I crashed while alone in the woods and didn't have a computer with crash detection. So I decided to get a Garmin 1050 for the big screen and crash detection.  Fortunately I haven't needed it. But unfortunately it probably wouldn't have worked anyway. Twice now I've been going through the settings on my bike computer looking for something else and realized it said I didn't have an emergency contact so crash detection wouldn't work. It happened in March, and while I'm sure I had done it before, I redid my wife as emergency contact. And tested it to confirm the text message arrived. Just now I again found the computer said there wasn't an emergency contact and needed to set one up in the app. Checked and the app showed my wife with a verified phone number. I then verified her email and now the computer shows her verified and testing get assistance sends the phone text and email. And her phone shows the previous test from March. So I don't know when it broke, but at some point I lost that safety feature due to another Garmin bug. 

Feature bugs are one thing, but this is a safety bug. At least she would have my live track, which has never broken, but I hate that I bought a computer for a safety system that is too buggy to trust. (and I have no way of knowing whether the bug is the app or computer but the contact setup is in the app)

title: Doesn’t work well with iOS!!
text:
I live several states away from my mother so I was relieved to hear that I could locate her in an emergency. Except the GPS is lousy. It seems to reliably report if she’s home or “out and about” but it almost never tells me where she is exactly. Even when she’s home—and they have her address on her record—it puts her up to a couple miles away. Sometimes it says she’s in another city. A few times she’s been in the middle of a river! (And she doesn’t know how to swim.) 

After some searching I’ve learned that this has been a common glitch with iOS. You’d think this would be important enough to fix but apparently not. Luckily she’s not one to wander off (yet?) but if she ever were to do so this app would be useless.

title: “Lively Mobile +” with Fall Detection ✅
text:
Only three days after receiving my “Lively Mobile+” medical alert device, I bent over to pick up something small I had stepped on in my bare feet. 
The next thing I knew, I had crumpled and was sitting upright, on the floor, blankly looking around. (I’ve had a degenerative muscle condition for 30 years). 
I had began thinking “Well, That was unexpected!”
Then I heard a pleasant, confident voice greeting me by name… from my device:
“Mrs. Pearson your device indicates you had a fall. Are you alright?” Or something similar to that. She also asked several questions checking in my condition. Did I hit my head?, was I injured? etc. Which were all great because a hard fall can leave me befuddled a bit at first. 
Next she asked permission to put me on hold while she called Emergency Services and for me to please stay on the line. 
She was soon back to me and waited with me until Emergency Services showed up. The the call was pleasantly ended. 
Sign me: A Happy, Protected Customer
————
Note - the device runs on a full charge for approximately 80 hours. 
If it runs low, an unusual beep sounds … Even at 2:30 in the morning. 
I have decided mark Charging Days on my calendar until it is a habit. 
————
Special Note - I expected the device to be annoying to wear. I think I even wanted to hate it because it represented another stage of becoming more disabled. 
I was 100% wrong. 
Instead of being annoying, it is comfortable and I was surprised with how quickly I became adjusted to wearing it all the time. 
Favorite Detail about the “Lively Mobile+” model - My particular medical insurance paid for the device and all the monthly fees. 
If you’re considering this device, at least give your insurance company a call and see if it is covered or helpful on the costs. 
Since I live alone, my family and other loved ones are glad I took this step forward towards safety. They also like the free “Lively Link” app (shows clasped hands on the icon) where they can find out if I’ve had falls or been out and about. The GPS feature helps with that.
